eli: ran a ~30m nsys capture on prod-like load (mixed seq 32/256, batch 1-8). want a concise kernel hotspot ranking + occupancy suspects. attaching quick summary below — looking for which kernels we should prioritize for fusion/quant/tiling work.

marta: awesome, can you paste the top-by-total-gpu-time table? also include sm_efficiency and achieved_occupancy if available.

eli: pasted summary (extracted with `nsys stats --report summary`):
```
Total GPU time: 143.5s
1) aten_gemm_fwd (GEMM)        - 49.8s  (34.7%)  sm_eff=78%  occ=0.62
2) attn_forward_cuda           - 31.4s  (21.9%)  sm_eff=66%  occ=0.48
3) kv_cache_read               - 17.9s  (12.5%)  sm_eff=40%  occ=0.32
4) softmax_kernel              - 8.8s   (6.1%)   sm_eff=52%  occ=0.29
5) rng_kernel                  - 6.0s   (4.2%)   sm_eff=22%  occ=0.15
6) elementwise_add             - 5.4s   (3.8%)   sm_eff=45%  occ=0.28
7) memcpy_H2D                  - 4.4s   (3.1%)   (memcpy)
rest < 2% each
```

eli: notes: GEMM dominates obviously. attn_forward_cuda is the fused attention kernel we ship; kv_cache_read is our custom KV gather that shows poor occ at high seq. rng is curiously expensive (sampling path for temperature/beam).

rajan: quick thoughts — prioritize kernels with both high total time and low occupancy relative to sm_efficiency (i.e. low occupancy + moderate sm_eff => warp underutilization). kv_cache_read and rng_kernel look high ROI for optimization. Also check launch overhead for tiny batches; that kills occ.

rajan: run these quick filters: `nsys stats --report kernel | grep -E "aten_gemm|attn_forward_cuda|kv_cache_read|rng_kernel"` and then join with `nsys stats --report occupancy` to get occupancy per kernel.

eli: did that — attached single-shot numbers: `avg_blocks_per_sm` for kv_cache_read ~12 on A100, for attn_forward_cuda ~38, for gemm ~128.

marta: low blocks_per_sm for kv_cache_read explains 0.32 occ. For small seq/batch it's launch-limited. Consider batching policy: group requests with same seq into micro-batches to increase threads per block and reuse KV cache. Also consider doing a warp-level gather instead of thread-per-token.

sophie: I'll prototype a micro-batching shim in the runtime to aggregate small batch requests for KV reads. two quick experiments: 1) group-by-seq before dispatch, 2) lightweight kernel that does coalesced loads. Expect reduced kernel count and increased blocks_per_sm.

eli: good. for GEMM, we should check if cuBLAS matmul is already using split-K / tensor cores optimally at these shapes. If not, we might switch to cublasLt or our tuned fused GEMM path.

rajan: also flagging attn_forward_cuda — some warps idle due to variable seq-length tails. We could try packing sequences or dynamic tile sizing. The flakiness shows in perfetto timeline: attn forward spikes correlate with memcpy from host for prompt scoring.

eli: perf-ci-bot: upload of `nsys_capture_2156007890.qdrep` complete. Link: https://perf.ci/runs/2156007890

perf-ci-bot: regression check: comparing to baseline 2134440000 -> attn_forward_cuda time +8.7%, kv_cache_read +3.1%, overall GPU time +4.2%. Marking as "investigate".

marta: +1 on investigate. Can we get a breakdown by sequence length bucket? that will show whether 256-seq dominates GEMM or attn.

eli: added a quick bucket split (seq32 / seq256): GEMM 32s (seq256) + 17.8s (seq32) — so seq256 still heavier per request; attn 22.7s (seq256) + 8.7s (seq32). kv_cache_read is almost all seq256.

rajan: then plan: short term: micro-batching + warp-level gather for KV + reduce memcpy hotspots. Mid term: evaluate cublasLt for matmuls + tune attn tiling. Also get a small kernel heatmap (perfetto) with sample slices to validate.

eli: action items: 
- @sophie prototype micro-batching shim and warp-gather sketch (ETA 2d)
- @marta run cublasLt perf sweep on our GEMM shapes (ETA 3d)
- @rajan produce perfetto slice with annotated memcpy->attn correlations (ETA 1d)
- eli will re-run nsys on the shim + 1% traffic A/B once prototype ready

sophie: noted, will start today.

eli: thanks all — let's reconvene after the sweep. :thumbsup:
